citations.anchor: forbids an admin who is not a member of the workspace
citations.why: A second admin who holds workspaces:update but belongs to no workspace gets 403 on PATCH /api/workspaces/:id, and the row is asserted unchanged — the exact 'permission never substitutes for membership' claim.

citations.anchor: answers the same bytes for "not a member" and "no such workspace"
citations.why: Compares the full response bodies of a foreign workspace and a non-existent uuid across the /:id routes; any divergence in status or text fails it.

citations.anchor: a missing workspace and one you are not in read identically
citations.why: Covers the shell-screen half: the no-access screen renders the same for an unknown id as for a workspace the user is not in.

citations.anchor: returns only the workspaces the caller belongs to
citations.why: Two users in two workspaces each list GET /api/workspaces and the other's id is asserted absent. Pins the scoping clause; the structural 'no unscoped list exists in the read model' half is not pinned by any test.

citations.anchor: carries WorkspaceMemberGuard iff it names a workspace in the path
citations.why: Iterates every route WorkspacesModule.forRoot() mounts and asserts WorkspaceMemberGuard is present exactly on the path-scoped ones, so a new unguarded /workspaces/:id/… route fails.

citations.anchor: guards the two read-only preview counters too
citations.why: Names both entry-count routes explicitly and asserts each carries WorkspaceMemberGuard — the 'preview counters included' clause.

citations.anchor: throws on an empty id rather than passing it through
citations.why: Asserts the decorator throws instead of yielding a falsy/undefined workspace id; the sibling case covers the missing-guard path.

citations.anchor: removes the creator like any other member (no owner protection)
citations.why: The creator is removed through the ordinary member route and the workspace survives — pins 'no owner, the creator has no privileges'. The 'a membership row carries no role column' half is unpinned.

citations.anchor: refuses to remove the last member (no-memberless-workspace)
citations.why: The aggregate itself throws LastMemberError when the only membership is removed — the rule is asserted on the domain object, not on a route.

citations.anchor: is refused, leaving the workspace reachable
citations.why: DELETE of the last membership answers 409 over HTTP and the workspace is still listed afterwards — the LastMemberError → 409 translation end to end.

citations.anchor: a no-op raises nothing (the other half of idempotence)
citations.why: A block of cases (addMember, removeMember, grantContent, revokeContent, a refused change) each assert the mutator reports no change and pulls no domain event.

citations.anchor: turns the slug unique violation into SlugTakenError
citations.why: A driver-level unique-constraint error out of the insert is asserted to surface as the domain SlugTakenError (which the filter maps to 409) rather than propagating as a 500.

citations.anchor: yields exactly one 201 and 409s the losers, never a 500
citations.why: Concurrent creates on one slug: exactly one 201, the rest 409, no 5xx, one row in the database — the unique index as arbiter.

citations.anchor: accepts lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens
citations.why: The server-side rule is asserted on the Slug value object itself (accepted corpus plus the 120/121 boundary), not on a DTO decorator.

citations.anchor: Slug (admin mirror of the server rule)
citations.why: Runs the server spec's corpus — including the near-misses blog_post and 121 characters — against the admin Slug VO, so a drift between the two rules fails.

citations.anchor: 'rejects %s', (_label, value) => {
citations.why: Six off-palette values (hex, css token, wrong case, padded, empty) each throw InvalidWorkspaceColorError, while the sibling case accepts every WORKSPACE_COLORS key — an arbitrary string cannot become a colour.

citations.anchor: rejects a color outside the seven-key palette
citations.why: POST /api/workspaces with 'chartreuse' and '#bada55' both answer 400 — the palette is closed at the route, not only in the VO.

citations.anchor: has no slug property at all
citations.why: Asserts UpdateWorkspaceDto declares no slug, and the neighbouring cases assert a body carrying one is rejected by the whitelisting ValidationPipe.

citations.anchor: rejects a slug in the patch body and leaves the slug alone
citations.why: PATCH with a slug is refused and the stored slug is re-read unchanged — no other route accepts one.

citations.anchor: refuses (409) to delete a workspace that still has content entries
citations.why: The delete half: a workspace holding entries answers 409 and is still there afterwards.

citations.anchor: refuses (409) to revoke a type that still has entries in the workspace
citations.why: The revoke half: DELETE /workspaces/:id/content/:slug answers 409 while the type holds entries and the grant survives.

citations.anchor: refuses both destructive routes with 503 while the counters read 0
citations.why: Boots a second app without the content plugin over the same database: both entry-count reads still answer 200 {count: 0} while DELETE workspace and DELETE grant both answer 503 — exactly the two clauses.

citations.anchor: takes the exclusive lock, not the shared one entry writes take
citations.why: Renders the SQL findByIdForContentMutation issues and asserts pg_advisory_xact_lock( and not pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared, plus a sibling case that findById takes no lock at all. The 'writing an entry takes the shared one' clause lives in content/server and workspace-lock.ts and is not unit-pinned.

citations.anchor: loads under the content lock, never through the plain reader
citations.why: Asserts the delete use case reaches for findByIdForContentMutation and never findById — the locking loader is what deletion uses.

citations.anchor: loads under the content lock, never through the plain reader
citations.why: The same assertion for grant revocation, the second operation the invariant names.

citations.anchor: purges inside the unit of work and before the workspace row goes
citations.why: Records the call order and asserts purgeAll runs within UnitOfWork.run and ahead of the workspace delete — the 'inside the transaction' clause.

citations.anchor: rolls everything back when one purger throws
citations.why: Registers a throwing purger and asserts the workspace and every other plugin's rows are still present after the failed delete.

citations.anchor: runs the reclaim thunk only after the run resolves
citations.why: Asserts reclaim has not fired while the unit of work is open and does fire once it commits; siblings assert it never fires when the transaction or a purger fails.

citations.anchor: swallows a reclaim failure — the rows are already committed
citations.why: A throwing reclaim resolves rather than rejects, and the other contributor's reclaim still runs — the 'logged and swallowed' clause.

citations.anchor: refuses a duplicate name rather than double-counting it
citations.why: register() with a name already taken throws /Duplicate workspace purger "media"/ and the registry keeps one entry — a silent overwrite would fail both assertions.

citations.anchor: derives the kind from the catalogue rather than the request
citations.why: The kind written is the catalogue's, not anything the request carried; the sibling case asserts an unknown slug is rejected before the unit of work opens.

citations.anchor: 400s for an unknown content-type slug
citations.why: The 400 half over HTTP: POST /workspaces/:id/content with a slug the catalogue does not know is refused.

citations.anchor: expands to one row per known slug, collections before pages
citations.why: mode 'all' resolves to an explicit grant row for every catalogue slug; the sibling cases assert an unknown slug is dropped rather than granted, so a row always means an explicit grant.

citations.anchor: commits the change, holds the event, and audits it on recovery
citations.why: With the dispatcher suspended, the workspace is created AND an undispatched workspace.created outbox row exists while the activity table has none — an inline audit write or an out-of-transaction event would fail one of the two. The 'no inline calls to the audit recorder' clause is structural and unpinned.

citations.anchor: imports nothing from %s
citations.why: Reads every non-spec file under domain/ and asserts no import specifier matches @nestjs/*, drizzle-orm, class-validator or infrastructure — all four prohibitions, with a guard case proving the file list is non-empty.

citations.anchor: does not re-export the users stub under any name
citations.why: Asserts the barrel's exports are exactly the three owned tables and that no export is the users stub, which is what keeps drizzle-kit from emitting a second CREATE TABLE users.

citations.anchor: normalises and de-dupes an address, issuing one lookup and one insert
citations.why: One address in two cases produces a single lookup and a single insert; a sibling asserts a stored address matches case-insensitively on the way back.

citations.anchor: provisions one account and one membership for an address invited twice
citations.why: End to end: the same address invited twice yields one users row and one membership, not two.

citations.anchor: drops an id the users table does not have, and still succeeds
citations.why: An unresolvable directory id is discarded and the provisioner resolves rather than throwing.

citations.anchor: drops a member id that resolves to no user, and still creates
citations.why: POST /api/workspaces carrying a phantom member id still answers 201 and the workspace exists — no foreign-key failure reaches the caller.

citations.anchor: filters on nothing but the id — an archived workspace still exists
citations.why: Asserts the emitted query carries no status predicate, so the WORKSPACE_DIRECTORY port answers existence and an archived workspace stays a legitimate token scope.

citations.anchor: never touches api_tokens — narrowing a scope is not revoking a token
citations.why: Asserts the purger's only delete is against api_token_workspaces and api_tokens is never written.

citations.anchor: drops the workspace from a token bucket without revoking the token
citations.why: After deleting a scoped workspace the token row survives and still works against its other workspaces.

citations.anchor: gates the slug-availability probe on workspaces:create
citations.why: Asserts GET /workspaces/slug-available declares exactly [WORKSPACES_CREATE]; dropping the decorator to leave it merely authenticated fails it.

citations.anchor: 403s the slug probe for a role that cannot create
citations.why: A signed-in role without workspaces:create gets 403 from the probe, and a sibling case asserts a role that can create is served.

citations.anchor: counter matches its action's permission
citations.why: Asserts each preview counter's permission list equals its action route's, as a pairing rather than a literal — re-gate the action alone and it fails.

citations.anchor: serves the per-type count to workspaces:update and refuses the workspace count
citations.why: A purpose-built role holding only workspaces:update reads the per-type counter (200) and is refused the workspace counter (403) — the split observed over HTTP.

citations.anchor: says the list could not be loaded rather than showing nothing
citations.why: With isError set, the sidebar quick-list renders the load-failed copy; a sibling asserts it still does so for a user who could create one.

citations.anchor: the list page alerts, withholds the empty copy, and retries
citations.why: With /api/workspaces failing, the page shows the error alert and 'No workspaces yet' is asserted hidden — the exact misreading the invariant forbids.

citations.anchor: allows the action only on a known zero, with no warning shown
citations.why: The confirm button is enabled for count 0 and disabled for loading, error, undefined and count > 0 across the neighbouring cases — precisely the 'only on a known zero' rule.

citations.anchor: blocks the action when the count could not be read
citations.why: The 'the check failed' half of the pair the invariant names explicitly, asserted separately from the 'still checking' case.

citations.anchor: blocks Delete when the content check cannot be read
citations.why: End to end on the real dialog: with the count endpoint failing, Delete stays disabled and the 'we could not check' copy is shown.

citations.anchor: reports a failed check as Unknown, never Available
citations.why: A failing slug request resolves to the Unknown state, asserted not to be Available — the hook cannot fail open.

citations.anchor: reports the check failed and keeps Continue disabled
citations.why: The wizard's step transition stays blocked when the availability probe errors — the 'does not unlock the move to the next step' clause.

citations.anchor: refuses a deep link to the Danger zone at the route
citations.why: Navigating straight to settings/danger without the permission lands on settings/general, renders no danger control, writes the explanation into the live region and moves focus to main — the route half plus the explanation.

citations.anchor: hides edit controls and the danger tab
citations.why: The tab half: a viewer sees read-only fields and no Danger zone tab in the section nav.
